title: Anthropic opens at $111.50 on Nasdaq, closes $97.17 — largest IPO on record
subtitle: ANT priced at $83 the night before, opened 34% above offering, briefly cleared a $2 trillion market cap intraday, then faded to a 17% first-day gain and a $1.75 trillion fully diluted close.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq under ticker ANT on Thursday, November 19, 2026. The company priced its offering at $83 the night before — above the filed $70 to $78 range — and Class A shares opened at $111.50, roughly 34% above the offering price. The stock briefly carried the company past a $2 trillion market capitalization during the session before fading, and closed at $97.17, up about 17% on the day. Forbes puts the fully diluted close at about $1.75 trillion. The raise is the largest IPO on record, ahead of the $75 billion SpaceX offering in June.

The intraday fade matters as much as the open. A 34% pop that gives back half its gain by the close signals that institutional allocators got the shares they wanted at the open, and the aftermarket then traded on fundamentals rather than scarcity. That is a healthier first-day tape than a straight ramp, because it tells future AI issuers — OpenAI chief among them — that the public market will absorb size at a premium but will not pay any price for it. The $1.75 trillion close also matches, rather than exceeds, Anthropic's last private-market indication, so this is a calibration event, not a repricing.

The week that produced this print is the capital-market test of the AI cycle. NVIDIA's blowout Q3 on Monday, OpenAI's GPT-6.2 launch Tuesday, and Anthropic's debut Thursday together answer three different questions — is the infrastructure delivering, is the frontier still advancing, and will the public market fund the safety-first lab at scale. The answer this week was yes to all three. The next test is OpenAI's filing, which the company has signaled for Q1 2027, and whether ANT holds the $1.75 trillion line through the lock-up expiration in May.

For learners: a first-day close above the offering price but well below the opening price is the shape of a well-run IPO. The underwriters got price discovery, insiders got liquidity at a premium, and the public shareholders who bought at the open paid for the scarcity rather than the fundamentals. If you are trying to read AI valuations in the next six months, watch the ANT chart against the Nasdaq-100 and against OpenAI's eventual S-1 — the relative move will tell you more than any single headline number.
